  1. The Rust borrow checker is the part of the compiler that enforces safe use of references by making sure they always point to valid data. While a reference exists, Rust prevents the referenced object from being destroyed, and it also blocks unsafe cases like mutating data at the same time it’s borrowed.

    Rust Programming Language

    https://doc.rust-lang.org › beta › rust-by-example › scope › borrow.html

    Borrowing - Rust By Example

    Borrowing Most of the time, we'd like to access data without taking ownership over it. To accomplish this, Rust uses a borrowing mechanism. Instead of passing objects by value (T), objects can be passed by reference (&T). The compiler statically guarantees (via its borrow checker) that references always point to valid objects.
